english: Stranger, why do you follow my sheep? I caught sight of a wolf by the path. I am protecting you. I do not tremble before wolves; I have a big dog. Your dog is lying under the tree. I will walk to the village, and I will lift your lamb. What is your name, stranger? I am Of-Good-Horses. And what is your name? Kindly. Come to our house in the morning.

english: Father, I will lead home the daughter of Of-Good-Horses. She is the most beautiful of the women. A flower is beautiful in the spring, and in the summer it is dry. Is she wise? I do not know. I have not spoken to her. Speak to her, and look at her hands. Which wife did you choose? I chose your mother. She was not the most beautiful, but she was the wisest. And do you love her? I do love her. Now go and speak to the girl.

english: Husband, why are you looking at me? I remember that day. I saw you at the spring, and you were carrying water. In that summer I was young and beautiful. Now I am old. To me you are beautiful. Your heart is young. And you, old man, do you still cherish me? You are sweeter to me than honey. Sing me the old song. I will sing it, and you will sit by the hearth with me.

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis Héǵrom bʰugét.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: Old woman, you are wise. How does a man win a young woman? Gold does not win her. Listen to her, and what she says, remember it. And what does she want? She wants a man who will not leave his woman. I will not leave the woman; I promise. Do not promise to me; promise to her.

pie: eḱwos wewekur, "ḱludʰe, owei! ḱerd angʰetai widontbʰyos: ǵʰm̥on, potis, wl̥nam owiyōm kʷr̥neti soi gʷʰermom westrom; owibʰyos kʷe wl̥nā ne esti".
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: You forgot the feast of my kin! Why did you not go? I did not want it. A wolf came among the sheep in the night. Did it kill a ram? It killed none. I drove it away with my spear. Then I am not angry. Is your arm cut? My arm is cut. Come and sit by me. Let me wash your arm.

pie: kʷésmey swésor tód h₁rudʰróm usménōm téksi? ph₂tréy nos h₁íd ne téksmi. albʰóh₁eḱwōy? th₂kéh₁ye. méh₂tēr te ḱléweti. albʰóh₁eḱwōy-ge wésmn̥ téksi. wóyde? ne wóyde. h₁ésmey wésmn̥ sh₁séni déh₃oh₂. h₁yód h₁íd ne h₁áyetor? h₁íd h₁áyetor. spéḱyeti me.
english: Sister, for whom are you weaving that red garment? I am not weaving it for our father. Then for the one with the white horse? Be silent! Mother will hear you. So you are weaving the garment for the one with the white horse! Does he know? He does not know. I will give him the garment at harvest time. And if he does not take it? He will take it. He keeps looking at me.

pie: kʷíd toy usméni Hn̥dʰí ḱélesi? dóh₃r̥ toy. dr̥ḱdʰí. h₂r̥ǵn̥tósyo péh₃tlom. kʷíd moy h₂r̥ǵn̥tóm dédeh₃si? h₁eǵóh₂ ne h₃rēǵés dʰugh₂tḗr. túH moy h₂éh₂usōd h₁wésyōs. dh₂pnóy h₁ésmōd ph₃dʰí. ph₂tḗr moy préḱseti. kʷís toy ḱód péh₃tlom déh₃t? h₁ésmey wr̥h₁dʰí. poh₂imnés suHnús h₁íd déh₃t. h₁ím wésni gʷm̥yóh₂. nu gʷm̥dʰí gʷṓs-kʷe bʰére.
english: What are you hiding under your garment? Your gift. Look! A cup of silver. Why do you give me silver? I am not a king's daughter. To me you are better than gold. Drink from it at the feast. My father will ask. "Who gave you this cup?" Tell him. The shepherd's son gave it. In the spring I will come to him. Come, then, and bring cows!

english: Of-Good-Horses, I have led a foal to you from my herd. The foal is swift. Why do you give it to me? The girl of your house is dear to me. A foal does not buy a wife. How many sheep do you have? Ten sheep and three goats. Lead the goats here, and in the spring we will speak again. I will lead them here; guard the foal. I will guard it. You are bold.

pie: méh₂ter nos mógʰus h₂egʷnóm stégos ḱósmi dinóy wédʰet. h₁ím widóm. h₁éy toy ḱéywos? h₁éy moy ḱéywos. h₁ésyo méh₂tr̥s dedwóyh₂e. h₁ésyeh₂s mē bʰéyh₂s. h₁wésus wiHrós h₁uséwih₂m gʷénh₂m̥ dṓm wédʰeti. kʷíh₁ h₁ésyo ḱḗr ǵnéh₃oh₂? h₁ésyo ǵʰóstoh₁ wékʷesh₂-kʷe spéḱye. h₁yós swṓys ǵʰóstōys wr̥ǵyéti só ne dʰrugʰyéti. wésmn̥ téksm̥. h₁ésmey h₁íd déh₃oh₂. dʰúgh₂ter moy h₁íd dh₃dʰí.
english: Mother, a young man led a lamb to our house today. I saw him. Is he dear to you? He is dear to me. But I am afraid of his mother. Do not be afraid of her. A good man leads a good wife home. How shall I know his heart? Watch his hands and his words. The man who works with his own hands does not deceive. I wove a garment. I will give it to him. Give it, my daughter.

pie: kʷíd h₁suménesos dʰwóri wékʷsperoy stestóh₂th₂e? h₂én stestóh₂h₂e h₁ésyeh₂ey-kʷe kéh₂nmn̥h₂ gʷéHyoh₂. kʷíd pr̥sḱési? h₁íh₂m̥ éti h₁íh₁eyǵʰmi. h₁eǵóh₂ twéd ḱéwh₁yōs. ḱuh₁rós h₂r̥Hmós gʷnéh₂s ḱḗr ne wént. nu h₁íh₂m̥ préḱsomes. kʷóterom lubʰyéti? préḱsomes. h₁yód twé wélh₁eti h₂epó gʷéh₂oh₂.
english: Why do you stand by the door of Kindly in the evening? I stand there and sing songs to her. Why do you ask? I desire her too. I am stronger than you. A strong arm does not win a woman's heart. Then let us ask her. Which of the two does she love? Let us ask. If she chooses you, I will go away.

pie: h₂ewsér wiHróysu médʰi h₁éysi? h₁éymi. gʷṓs dweh₂róns h₂éǵrons h₂éǵomes. kʷóm h₂éti gʷémesi? twé sh₁séni h₂éti gʷémoh₂. bʰoydʰéh₂m moy h₃m̥nh₃dʰí. dyéw moy ph₂ter h₁óytom ḱludʰí. h₂éti gʷm̥yṓh₂ dṓm-kʷe te wédʰōh₂. ménōh₂ te. gʰostísu me médʰi mē mérs. kʷíh₁ te mr̥syéh₁m̥? h₁nómn̥ toy moy ḱérdi h₁ésti.
english: At dawn you are going with the men? I am going. We are driving the cattle to the far pastures. When will you come back? At harvest time I will come back to you. Swear me an oath. Father Sky, hear my oath! I will come back, and I will lead you home. I will wait for you. Do not forget me among the strangers. How could I forget you? Your name is in my heart.

pie: pótni h₂éǵroybʰos h₂éti gʷegʷómh₂e. tísrn̥s nókʷtn̥s lelóykʷth₂e. h₁íh₁eyǵʰm̥ te. lówksneh₂m nékʷti spéḱyom h₁nómn̥-kʷe toy gʷéHyom. kénkesi? mḗms toy pékʷom. dérḱoh₂ te. túH lówksneh₂s ḱéwbʰyōs. pótey sweh₂dúh₂ wékʷesh₂ mléwHsi. nu h₁ddʰí. h₁édoh₂ méǵʰye-kʷe ḱóm sédesi.
english: Wife, I have come back from the pastures. You have been gone three nights! I longed for you. At night I looked at the moon and sang your name. Are you hungry? I have cooked meat for you. Let me look at you. You are more beautiful than the moon. You say sweet words, husband. Now eat! I will eat, and you will sit by me.

english: Grandfather, how did you win grandmother? Her brothers had swift horses. I yoked my two horses, and I ran against them. And did you win? I won: my horses were swifter than birds. And grandmother? She laughed and said: "Now win me." What did you do? For a year I sang to your grandmother in the evenings, and I still sing.

pie: kʷíd súHnew ne h₁ḗdsi? kʷéros toy pl̥h₁nós. ne kénkoh₂. swépnos h₁mé ne gʷm̥yéti. deywós te stunédt? h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂ me swṓys h₃kʷbʰís stunédt. kʷéh₂ h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂? h₁suḱléwesos swésōr. h₁íh₂ h₃reǵtéh₂. nu h₁ddʰí h₁ésyeh₂s-kʷe méh₂trey h₂éyeri bʰéh₂oh₂. nu h₁édoh₂.
english: Son, why do you not eat? Your pot is full. I am not hungry. And sleep does not come to me. Has a god struck you? A girl struck me with her eyes. Which girl? The sister of Of-Good-Fame. She is upright. Eat now, and in the morning I will speak to her mother. Then I will eat.

english: What is on your loom, Of-True-Fame? My brother's garment. Will you give me a belt? Belts I give to my husband alone. Then choose me as your husband. Ask my three brothers first. They are strong. I am not afraid of your brothers. Then they will grow fond of you.

english: Look, woman: I bring you gold and a silver cup. Your gift is great. But I will not take it. Why will you not take it? Of-True-Fame has three sheep and an old dog. But Of-True-Fame sings for me, and his heart is true. I too will sing for you. Sing, then. But a song that one buys with gold is not sweet. Then I will seek a woman over yonder. Go, and may the gods give you a good wife.

english: Sister, why does Fame-from-the-Gods drive his cattle to our spring? His cattle are thirsty. Why do you ask, brother? There is water in the river too. But he drives his herd here, and he looks at you. Be silent, brother! You say too many words. If you give me honey, I will be silent. Take the honey, and say nothing to our father.

english: Daughter, Man-Minded has asked for you. Do you want him as your husband? He has much wealth, and his words are good. But he is old, father. An old husband protects his wife. I do not want him. I want a young man who will laugh with me. Who is he? The son of the shepherd. In the spring he brought you a lamb. A lamb is not ten cows. But I will speak with his father.

pie: dwóh₁ te h₂nérh₁e h₁r̥h₁tā́m. kʷóterom wélh₁esi? polh₁éwes h₁éḱwōs h₁éterōy h₁sénti h₁éteros kh₂néti. h₃épnos dʰéh₁mn̥ h₂életi kéh₂nmn̥h₂ h₁íd ne h₂életi. h₃épnos ne kh₂néti. sweh₂dú kéh₂nmn̥ nókʷtm̥ gʷʰr̥néwti. h₁yós kh₂néti nu tóm wl̥h₁dʰí h₁éterom-kʷe moy dh₃dʰí. h₁ím sl̥h₂gʷdʰí h₁ésyo-kʷe h₁éḱwōys méwdoyh₁s.
english: Two men have asked for you. Which of the two will you choose? The one has many horses; the other sings. Wealth feeds a house; songs do not feed it. But wealth does not sing. And a sweet song warms the night. Then choose the one who sings, and give the other to me! Take him, and may you rejoice in his horses.

english: Why are you red, Of-Goodly-Fame? The sun is burning. The sun? Evening has come! Then desire is burning me. I know. Why do you tremble? I am not a wolf. You are not a wolf, but I am a lamb. Then come, lamb, and walk with me to the spring.

pie: kʷíd ǵérh₂ont wékʷsperoy h₁idʰé sédyesi? pótnih₂ moy dʰǵʰémi h₁idʰé ḱéyor. h₁íh₂m̥ memónh₂e solh₂wóybʰos h₁suménēs h₁ést. mā́dsoh₁ moy polh₁úh₂ yéh₁ōr pékʷet séngʷʰet-kʷe moy. ḱlush₁yéti te? pótn̥yeh₂ey moy h₂mélǵos mélit-kʷe h₁opéyoh₂ ḱlush₁yóyh₁t me. deywṓs h₁íh₂m̥ ph₂sih₁ént. h₁íh₂m̥ gʷh₂yéh₁m̥.
english: Old man, why do you sit here every evening? My wife lies here in the earth. I remember her: she was kind to all. Many years she cooked food for me and sang to me. Does she hear you? I bring my wife milk and honey; may she hear me. May the gods guard her. And may I go to her.

pie: gʰóstey moy swésorm̥ h₂isḱési. túH dʰr̥sús? h₂ŕ̥tḱom pérunsu péruti gʷʰénm̥. ǵʰoysóm moy toy déyḱe. ḱós moy ǵʰoysós. swésorm̥ moy toy déh₃esi? h₁íh₂m̥ ne dédeh₃mi ǵérh₂ontes h₁íh₂m̥ dédh₃n̥ti. ǵʰoysóm toy h₁énod dóru Hih₁kdʰí. h₁ím Hyéh₁km̥ dréwi-kʷe stestóh₂e. h₂r̥Hmós toy tewh₂séh₂m. dʰh₁tléh₂i te gʷr̥néHoh₂.
english: Stranger, you are seeking my sister. Are you bold? Last year I killed a bear in the mountains. Show me your spear. This is my spear. Will you give me your sister? I do not give her; the elders give her. But first throw your spear at that tree. I have thrown it, and it stands in the tree. Your arm is strong. I will praise you in the assembly.

pie: h₃réǵ deywóǵenh₁esm̥ pr̥sḱóh₂. kʷód toy h₃épnos h₁ésti? ne kʷid moy h₁ésti. ǵʰóstoh₁ moy ish₁róh₁. ish₁róh₁ ǵʰóstoh₁ ne h₁wédmn̥. h₂ówins toy tísrn̥s sémās péh₂soh₂. tísrn̥s sémās ménēti? ménēti h₁óytom bʰr̥h₁wéni h₃m̥nh₃wé. nu moy stéh₂dʰh₁om ph₂sdʰí ǵʰóstoh₁-kʷe toy dérḱomes.
english: King, I ask for Of-Divine-Race. What wealth do you have? I have nothing. But my hands are strong. Strong hands are not a bride-price. I will guard your sheep for three summers. Will she wait three summers? She will wait: we swore an oath at the spring. Then guard my herd, and we shall look at your hands.

pie: kʷíd príHe bʰéwdʰesi? h₂élyōs ssénti. swépnos méd bʰéwgt. gʷnéh₂s h₃ókʷih₁ memónh₂e. kʷésyo h₃ókʷih₁? ǵʰh₂n̥sṓm h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂s. ǵʰh₂énsn̥s léymonm̥ h₂éyeri h₂éǵeti. nu léymonm̥ h₂éyeri h₁idʰí tósyeh₂ey-kʷe mluHdʰí. kʷíd sokʷéyōh₂? sokʷéye. ǵʰh₂énses toy albʰéh₂es túH-kʷe téh₂bʰos h₂érǵyōs. h₂ewsér sokʷéyōh₂.
english: Why are you awake, friend? The others are asleep. Sleep flees from me. I remember a woman's eyes. Whose eyes? The goose-girl's. In the morning she drives the geese to the lake. Then go to the lake in the morning and speak to her. And what shall I say? Say: "Your geese are white, and you are brighter than they." I will speak at dawn.

pie: owis, yesmin wl̥nā ne ēst, dedorḱe eḱwons wogʰom gʷr̥um wegʰontn̥s, bʰorom meǵHm, monum ōḱu bʰerontn̥s.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: kʷíh₁ príHe deywóǵenh₁esos dʰugh₂tréy h₂roh₁dʰéyōh₂? h₁íh₂m̥ gʰr̥yési? h₁íh₂m̥ gʰr̥yóh₂. h₁yód h₁íh₂m̥ widṓh₂ dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s moy th₂kéh₁yeti. nu mē h₂roh₁dʰéyes. h₁ésyeh₂ey déh₃rom dh₃dʰí h₁íh₂m̥-kʷe dr̥ḱdʰí. kʷód déh₃rom? h₂éwyōm toy h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m. gʷénh₂es h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m gʰr̥yónti. péh₂ureh₂-kʷe wékʷesh₂ mluHdʰí. h₁yód sméyeti? nu te gʰr̥yéti. h₁yéh₂ smḗyti séh₂ ne gʰrémeti.
english: Friend, how shall I speak to the daughter of Of-Divine-Race? Do you desire her? I desire her. But when I see her, my tongue is silent. Then do not speak. Give her a gift, and look at her. What gift? The wool of your sheep. Women like wool. And say few words. And if she laughs? Then she likes you. A girl who laughs is not angry.
